item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q004_ferritin_like_functional_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, these proteins are separate families within the same ferritin-like superfamily (a.25.1) and ferritin-like fold (a.25): ferritin is a.25.1.1 (SUNID 47241), ribonucleotide-reductase-like proteins are a.25.1.2 (SUNID 47253), and manganese catalase is a.25.1.3 (SUNID 100951). Sharing a superfamily supports probable remote common ancestry—not merely analogous folding—but the family split marks substantial divergence. Their conserved helical, often dinuclear-metal scaffold therefore does not justify transferring chemistry: ferritin iron storage/ferroxidase activity, ribonucleotide-reductase radical/cofactor chemistry, and manganese-catalase peroxide disproportionation are not interchangeable annotations. A structure from another family may serve as a remote fold/template guide, but active-site geometry, metal identity, substrate specificity, oligomeric assembly, and function should not be copied; prefer a representative from the same family and a closer sequence context. Assignment of a new protein's chemistry requires external evidence such as family-specific sequence/profile and catalytic-residue conservation, detailed structural/metal-site comparison, and biochemical cofactor and activity assays; SCOPe placement alone is insufficient.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info — /api/v1/, /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop — /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=manganese+catalase&mode=auto&limit=20","mcp__scope__get_scop_node — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/a.25.1/parents","mcp__scope__list_scop_children — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47240/children?limit=100"]}]}
